acme-sre: Hey team — starting ~10:02 UTC our /v1/embeddings responses switched to vectors of length 128 instead of the expected 1536. Search quality dropped. Request id: req_01F8TRX. p99 latency moved from ~80ms -> ~1.2s. Any quick checks?

tara: Thanks @acme-sre. Can you paste a sample response (headers ok) and confirm project/org id + SDK version?

acme-sre: Sample curl we used:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-XXXX" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"open-embed-lite","input":["hello"]}'
```
Response snippet we saw:
```json
{
  "data": [{"embedding": [0.12, 0.03, ...], "length": 128}],
  "meta": {"request_id": "req_01F8TRX", "model": "open-embed-lite-v0.3", "served_by": "gpu-34"}
}
```

liam: Hmm — looks like the request was served by a low-dim variant. @sre-bot can you paste the trace for req_01F8TRX?

sre-bot: Trace: https://console.redwood.ai/traces/req_01F8TRX — path shows: embeddings.route -> batch-coalescer -> model-fallback(lowdim). Notice tag: batch_size=32 and model_swap=true. batch_coalescer latency ~950ms.

tara: Can you confirm whether your app set any batching headers or used the batch endpoint? Also which SDK (v)? Quick repro: try a single request with batching disabled: set header `X-Batching: none` or send single-input with batch_size=1.

acme-sre: We didn't intentionally set batching — using SDK v0.9.2 defaults. Quick test with batching disabled:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-XXXX" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -H "X-Batching: none" \n  -d '{"model":"open-embed-lite","input":"hello"}'
```
Result: embedding length 1536, latency ~85ms. So disabling batching returns correct dims immediately.

liam: That points to the coalescer/batcher combining requests into a batch which triggers autoswitch to a lower-capacity variant (lowdim) to keep latency under a burst SLO. We should check the binpack policy and fallback thresholds.

tara: I've opened INC-4582 and applied a short-term mitigation: pinned the customer's route to `open-embed-lite@v0.3` (the full-dim variant) for 30 minutes to restore service. Also added a dashboard panel that shows per-request `model_variant` and `batch_size` histogram. Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/emb-route-splits

acme-sre: :thumbsup: After pinning we reverted to 1536 dims and search latency recovered. Appreciate the fast help. Any recommended request flags to prevent autoswitch?

liam: You can either pin in the console or send routing in the request body, e.g.
```json
{"model":"open-embed-lite@v0.3","routing":{"allow_autoswitch":false}}
```
Or set app-level config to disable autoswitch for that route. We'll also add a more explicit SDK option.

tara: Action items: ENG to review coalescer binpack config and fallback thresholds; OPS to check GPU pool overflow/pressure around 10:00-10:10; Support to update runbook with quick commands: how to fetch trace + how to pin model.

acme-sre: Sharing the extracted timeline from the trace for postmortem:
```
[10:02:12] receive -> enqueue (queue_size=28)
[10:02:12] batch formed (size=32) -> routing decision -> fallback to lowdim variant
[10:02:13] lowdim serve complete (latency 950ms)
```

james: FYI I added a dashboard alert: if >5% of requests for a route return dim != expected within 5m, create an incident to #incidents. That should catch future regressions earlier.

acme-sre: Thanks all — will keep monitoring and will reach back if anything recurrence shows up.
